newsitem.title: FINLAND: ETLA SEES FINLAND BANK SHADOWING BUBA, NO '97 HIKE.
newsitem.headline: ETLA SEES FINLAND BANK SHADOWING BUBA, NO '97 HIKE.

text.p: The Research Institute of the Finnish Economy (ETLA) expects the Bank of Finland's monetary policy to track the Bundesbank's, and thinks the German central bank is unlikely to hike key interest rates this year.

In a monthly report dated April 29 and received on Wednesday, ETLA said: "the tightening of monetary policy this year is regarded as unlikely. Finnish monetary policy follows German monetary policy more closely than before."
The Bank of Finland's key monetary policy tool -- the tender rate -- has been on par with the Bundesbank's repo rate at 3.00 percent since October.

"Economic developments in Germany in the beginning of this year would tend to indicate that the Bundesbank will be unwilling to risk falling short of the EMU criteria on public finances by tightening monetary policy," ETLA said. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
